subject: Decision: low-p99 latency vs sustained throughput - VertexHealth
messages:
From: Alexandra Li <alex.li@vertexhealth.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Torres <michael.torres@vertexhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 18:22:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment trade-offs follow-up: latency vs sustained throughput

Hi Priya —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap from our side and a couple of clarifying questions before we commit to a PoC:

- Primary goal: 99th percentile latency <= 80ms for single-user interactive flows (chat assist) at model context ~2k tokens.
- Secondary: sustained background batch scoring at ~5k QPS for embedding/rerank pipelines during batch windows.
- Data residency: PHI will be involved for some endpoints — we need to understand Private/VPC options and KMS support.

Attached is a spreadsheet with example traffic shapes and the latency targets per endpoint (vertex_latency_requirements.xlsx).

Questions we have:
1) For the latency SLO above, should we evaluate Hosted API first or go straight to Dedicated?
2) If Dedicated, what level of reserved capacity do you recommend for the 80ms p99 at peak (we're expecting 50 concurrent low-latency sessions)?
3) What does the benchmark/PoC window look like (length, metrics, who runs it)?

Appreciate any suggested next steps and an outline of trade-offs. We’re hoping to finalize procurement timelines in the next two weeks.

Best,
Alexandra
Alexandra Li
Director, Product — VertexHealth
Attachments: vertex_latency_requirements.xlsx

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Alexandra Li <alex.li@vertexhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment trade-offs follow-up: latency vs sustained throughput

Hi Alexandra —

Thanks for the clear summary and for sharing the spreadsheet. Appreciate the explicit SLOs — that helps narrow options. Short answers up front, then proposed next steps below.

High-level recommendation
- For your interactive chat flows (p99 <= 80ms, ~2k context, ~50 concurrent sessions): Dedicated capacity is the conservative path to hit p99 consistently, especially if you plan larger model sizes (7B+).
- Hosted API can meet your needs for initial validation and early launch if you accept short warm-up variance and leverage prefix caching + our accelerated kernels, but p99 guarantees are weaker under bursty concurrency.
- Private VPC makes sense if PHI pathways require customer-managed network and KMS; otherwise Dedicated (with private tenancy) often suffices.

Questions from our side
1) Model family and size for both chat and batch scoring? (e.g., Llama2-70B, MPT-7B, custom fine-tuned).
2) Typical token lengths for scoring batch jobs and max context for chat.
3) Expected growth curve over 3 months (so we can size reserved pools).

Proposed PoC plan - Step 0: Confirm model(s) and dataset slices (action: Vertex) - Step 1: 48-hour hosted baseline (Hosted API) to capture cold/warm behavior and token distribution (action: Redwood — Ben runs) - Step 2: 48-72 hour Dedicated run (self-hosted in Redwood reserved pool) to validate steady-state p99 and throughput (action: Redwood — infra + Karthik) - Step 3: If PHI flows are required, we run a short Private VPC gating test (action: Redwood + Vertex security)

Deliverables and timeline- Benchmark report with p50/p95/p99, tail-latency plots, and token-cost delta: delivered within 5 business days of test completion.
- Recommended committed capacity and monthly cost estimate (we'll include quantization options).

Next steps for this week- You: confirm model family/size and whether PHI will be in-scope for the initial PoC.
- We: prepare Dedicated estimate and a hosted baseline plan (I’ll attach the cost sketch).

Attaching an updated Dedicated estimate (redwood_dedicated_estimate_v2.pdf). Happy to hop on a 30-min call to finalize PoC entry criteria.

Thanks —
Priya Natarajan
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Cell: (415) 555-0199
Redwood Inference

From: Michael Torres <michael.torres@vertexhealth.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Alexandra Li <alex.li@vertexhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 6 May 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment trade-offs follow-up: latency vs sustained throughput

Priya/Ben/Karthik —

Thanks for the thorough notes. Quick answers:
- Models: Chat: fine-tuned Llama-2-13B; Batch scoring: distilled embedding model (2B).
- Token lengths: chat avg around 650 tokens, max ~2,200. Batch records are smaller, ~128 tokens each.
- PHI: yes, a subset of chat traffic will include PHI in the initial integration — we need KMS and VPC options documented.
- Growth: expect concurrency to ramp from ~50 to ~250 over 3 months if initial launch metrics hold.

We’re happy to proceed with the 48-hour hosted baseline first, then move to Dedicated testing. Please send PoC schedule and acceptance criteria and we’ll get procurement engaged.

-Michael
Michael Torres
Senior Eng Manager, VertexHealth
